problems.reason: Both sentences refer to the name Metriacanthosaurus as a synonym of Becklespinax, repeating the same claim.
Sentence 4 estimates Altispinax as a one‑tonne predator, while sentence 12 describes it as a large predatory theropod, implying a much larger size.
Sentence 10 claims the type specimen is a tooth that is not diagnostic, whereas sentences 1 and 2 state the holotype is a set of three posterior dorsal vertebrae.
Sentence 11 discusses the genus Becklespinax and its species, which is a separate taxon; it is presented as if it were about Altispinax itself.
Refers to vertebrae closest to the skull and an injury to a back frill, but the holotype contains only three posterior dorsal vertebrae and no frill is described.
Discusses a gap between front spines, yet the holotype consists of only posterior dorsal vertebrae, leaving the front spines undefined.
Describes the naming of a new genus (Becklespinax) and a synonym (Metriacanthosaurus) rather than providing information about Altispinax itself.
